title: Interpol joins search for missing Edmonton children as father faces kidnapping charges
summary: Edmonton police say they are working with international agencies to locate an Edmonton man, who has been charged with kidnapping, and his two children.

image.caption: Edmonton police say they are working with international agencies to locate Scot MacDermid, who has been charged with kidnapping, and his two children. (CBC)

blocks.text: Edmonton·New
Edmonton police say they are working with international agencies to locate an Edmonton man, who has been charged with kidnapping, and his two children.
Police say Scot MacDermid may have already left Canada or could try to leave the country.
Edmonton police say they are working with international agencies to locate an Edmonton man, who has is facing kidnapping charges, and his two children.
Edmonton Police Service said in a news release Friday that charges have also been laid against three more people accused of obstructing an investigation in the case.

Canada-wide warrants were issued in September for 43-year-old Scot MacDermid (also spelled Macdermid) in the alleged abduction of his son, George, 6, and daughter, Lesley, 9. He was initially wanted for abduction in contravention of a custody order, but he now faces two counts of kidnapping.
Missing children Lesley, 9, and George, 6. Their father, Scot MacDermid, is now wanted on Canada-wide warrants in their disappearance. (Edmonton Police Service)
MacDermid is also wanted on additional warrants for two counts of child endangerment, intimidation, assault causing bodily harm and 18 firearms-related offences.
Those charges against MacDermid relate to events in 2022, according to police.

Police say officers have also identified a man they were previously seeking in connection with the investigation. He faces two counts of abduction in contravention of a custody order and one count of obstructing a peace officer.
Two women have also been charged, both with obstructing a peace officer. One of the women faces an additional charge of possession of stolen property valued at more than $5,000.
Police said they have identified other people suspected of helping MacDermid evade authorities and will be contacting them.

“MacDermid continues to evade authorities at the expense of his children’s welfare, and we are encouraging him to turn himself in as soon as possible,” Staff Sgt. Robert Davis of Edmonton Police Service's child protection section said in the news release.
“As well, police believe that there are persons in Canada and abroad providing aid and comfort to Scot, and we are reminding them that doing so is a criminal offence.”

Scot MacDermid, 43, is wanted on Canada-wide warrants in relation to the alleged abduction of his children. Edmonton police say the background of this image was modified using AI so it could be shared with the public. (Edmonton Police Service)

Police are working with international agencies on the investigation and believe MacDermid may have already left Canada or could try to leave the country. Police have previously said MacDermid and the two children were last seen in late August.
EPS investigators have engaged Interpol, which has issued a Yellow Notice — a global police alert used to help locate missing people.
Investigators are asking anyone with information about MacDermid or the children's whereabouts to contact police.
